questions.stem: Which list contains only renewable energy resources?

options.text: wind, hydroelectricity, geothermal, tidal
options.explanation: All four are replenished as fast as they are used.

options.text: coal, oil, natural gas
options.explanation: All three are fossil fuels — non-renewable.

options.text: nuclear fuel, wind, natural gas
options.explanation: Nuclear fuel and gas are non-renewable.

options.text: solar cells, coal, wave
options.explanation: Coal is non-renewable.

questions.stem: What makes an energy resource renewable?

options.text: it never needs a generator
options.explanation: Most renewables still drive turbines.

options.text: it is replenished at least as fast as it is used up
options.explanation: The rate of replacement matches or beats the rate of consumption.

options.text: it produces no carbon dioxide at all
options.explanation: Renewability is about replacement rate, not emissions.

options.text: it can be used in any country
options.explanation: Geography does not define renewability.

questions.stem: Which part is common to generating electricity from wind, water and fossil fuels?

options.text: a dam holding water at height
options.explanation: Only hydroelectric and tidal use dams.

options.text: sunlight focused on panels
options.explanation: Only solar resources use sunlight.

options.text: a turbine that turns a generator
options.explanation: Every turbine route shares that machinery.

options.text: burning fuel in a furnace
options.explanation: Wind and water burn nothing.

questions.stem: How do solar cells differ from every other resource on the list?

options.text: they can never be used on a large scale
options.explanation: Scale is not the difference named in the notes.

options.text: they store electricity for later use
options.explanation: Cells generate; they do not store.

options.text: they heat water in pipes for households
options.explanation: That is solar heating systems, the other solar technology.

options.text: they generate electricity without turning a turbine
options.explanation: Light is converted directly, no spinning shaft involved.

questions.stem: Why does reliable national electricity supply need a range of different resources?

options.text: each resource produces at different times, so a mix covers the gaps
options.explanation: Some resources only generate when wind, sun or tide cooperate.

options.text: a single resource would wear out the generators
options.explanation: Generators are shared machinery, not the constraint.

options.text: electricity from different resources is different
options.explanation: Electricity on the Grid is the same whatever made it.

options.text: the law requires at least three resources
options.explanation: No such rule is part of the physics.

questions.stem: State the definition of a renewable energy resource.
questions.modelAnswer: A renewable resource is an energy source that nature replenishes at least as quickly as we consume it, so it will not run out.

questions.stem: Name the two non-renewable energy resources named in these lessons.
questions.modelAnswer: The non-renewable resources are the fossil fuels — coal, oil and natural gas — and nuclear fuel.

questions.stem: Explain why solar heating panels cannot serve the National Grid's generating stations.
questions.modelAnswer: Solar heating panels are a heating technology: sunlight warms water in pipes inside the panel for households to use. No turbine or generator is involved, so no electricity is generated — that is the job of solar cells, which convert light directly.

questions.stem: A tidal barrage releases stored water that turns a turbine and then a generator. Trace the energy transfers from the stored water to the generator.
questions.modelAnswer: Energy passes from the raised water's gravitational potential store, into the moving water's kinetic store, then into the turbine's and finally the generator's kinetic store as electricity is generated.

questions.stem: What turns the turbines in a wind farm?

options.text: an electric motor driving the blades
options.explanation: The flow runs the other way — generation, not consumption.

options.text: the moving air itself
options.explanation: Wind strikes the blades and turns them directly.

options.text: steam from a boiler
options.explanation: Steam belongs to fossil, nuclear and geothermal routes.

options.text: falling water from a dam
options.explanation: That is the hydroelectric route.

questions.stem: Where does the energy chain begin in a hydroelectric station?

options.text: the thermal store of heated rocks
options.explanation: That is geothermal.

options.text: the nuclear store of the Sun
options.explanation: That opens the solar chains.

options.text: the gravitational potential store of the dammed water
options.explanation: Height is the opening deposit.

options.text: the kinetic store of the wind
options.explanation: That is the wind chain's start.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly traces the wind generation chain?

options.text: gravitational store, kinetic store, thermal store
options.explanation: No height and no heating appear in the wind chain.

options.text: nuclear store, thermal store, kinetic store
options.explanation: That resembles solar heating or fossil chains.

options.text: thermal store, kinetic store, thermal store
options.explanation: The wind chain contains no thermal link.

options.text: kinetic store of the wind, kinetic store of the turbine, kinetic store of the generator
options.explanation: Motion hands motion to motion along the chain.

questions.stem: What advantage does a hydroelectric dam have over a wind farm in matching supply to demand?

options.text: the dam releases its stored water whenever the Grid needs it
options.explanation: Stored height is dispatchable; the wind blows when it blows.

options.text: the dam's turbines spin without any energy transfer
options.explanation: Every spin is powered by falling water.

options.text: the wind farm can store its wind for later
options.explanation: Moving air cannot be banked.

options.text: the dam needs no generator
options.explanation: Both routes end in a generator.

questions.stem: In a hydroelectric dam, what happens to the water's energy as it falls towards the turbines?

options.text: its kinetic store fills the gravitational store
options.explanation: That is the filling direction of the dam, not the release.

options.text: its gravitational potential store empties into its kinetic store
options.explanation: Height converts to motion on the way down.

options.text: its kinetic store empties into its thermal store
options.explanation: The fall is not a heating process.

options.text: its stores stay unchanged until it hits the blades
options.explanation: The fall itself transfers energy.

questions.stem: State which store the energy chain starts from for wind generation.
questions.modelAnswer: The chain starts in the kinetic store of the moving wind, before passing to the turbine and the generator.

questions.stem: State where hydroelectric schemes store their water before it is released.
questions.modelAnswer: The water is stored at height, usually behind a dam, until it is released to turn the turbines.

questions.stem: Explain why the hydroelectric energy chain contains one more store than the wind chain.
questions.modelAnswer: Hydroelectric generation opens in the gravitational potential store of the raised water, which empties into the water's kinetic store as it falls; only then do the turbine and generator kinetic stores follow. Wind skips that opening conversion because the moving air already carries kinetic energy straight to the blades.

questions.stem: A tidal barrage is another water-based scheme. Describe how its generation chain parallels the hydroelectric one.
questions.modelAnswer: The barrage holds water at height at high and low tide, releases it to turn turbines directly, and those turbines turn a generator — so the chain again opens in the raised water's gravitational potential store and proceeds through kinetic stores of water, turbine and generator.

questions.stem: What heats the water in a geothermal power station?

options.text: sunlight focused on mirrors
options.explanation: No such stage appears in these notes.

options.text: the turbine's own motion
options.explanation: The turbine is downstream of the steam.

options.text: hot rocks underground
options.explanation: The rocks' thermal store does the heating.

options.text: burning natural gas
options.explanation: Gas is a separate fossil route.

questions.stem: Which store does the geothermal energy chain start from?

options.text: the kinetic store of the wind
options.explanation: That is the wind chain.

options.text: the gravitational store of dammed water
options.explanation: That is hydroelectric.

options.text: the nuclear store of the Sun
options.explanation: That opens the solar chains.

options.text: the thermal store of the hot rocks
options.explanation: Heat in the rocks is the opening deposit.

questions.stem: What is special about solar cells among the resources in these lessons?

options.text: they generate electricity without a turbine
options.explanation: Light converts directly; nothing spins.

options.text: they need the hottest water of any resource
options.explanation: No water is involved in a cell.

options.text: they are the only renewable resource
options.explanation: Wind, water and geothermal are renewable too.

options.text: they store sunlight for winter use
options.explanation: Cells convert; they do not store.

questions.stem: Which statement about solar heating panels is correct?

options.text: they cool houses in summer
options.explanation: Cooling is not in these notes.

options.text: they warm water in pipes for households to use
options.explanation: Heating, not generation, is their job.

options.text: they spin small turbines on rooftops
options.explanation: No turbine exists in a heating panel.

options.text: they generate electricity for the National Grid
options.explanation: Generation is the solar cells' role.

questions.stem: In which order does energy pass through stores in a geothermal station?

options.text: rocks kinetic, water thermal, turbine thermal
options.explanation: The rocks' store is thermal, and the turbine's is kinetic.

options.text: rocks thermal, water kinetic, turbine thermal
options.explanation: The steam's store at the turbine is kinetic.

options.text: rocks thermal, water thermal, turbine kinetic, generator kinetic
options.explanation: Heat boils water; steam spins the machinery.

options.text: water thermal, rocks thermal, generator kinetic
options.explanation: The rocks heat the water, not the reverse.

questions.stem: State what turns the turbines in a geothermal power station.
questions.modelAnswer: Steam, produced when cold water is heated by the underground hot rocks, turns the turbines.

questions.stem: State what solar cells use as their energy input.
questions.modelAnswer: Solar cells use energy from the Sun, in the form of sunlight, to generate electricity directly.

questions.stem: Explain why the geothermal chain passes through two thermal stores before reaching a kinetic one.
questions.modelAnswer: The energy begins as heat in the underground rocks and is transferred by heating into the pumped water, turning it to steam. Only once the steam flows at speed does its kinetic store drive the turbine, so two thermal stores precede the kinetic ones.

questions.stem: A school uses solar cells on its roof and a geothermal borehole in its grounds. State one difference in how the two deliver energy to the school.
questions.modelAnswer: The solar cells generate electricity directly from sunlight with no moving machinery, while the geothermal route heats water into steam that must spin a turbine and generator before electricity appears.
